holidays.name: Earth Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of the planet in which millions of people plant trees, clean up beaches, and pledge to finally remember their reusable shopping bags.
holidays.origin: First held in 1970 after Senator Gaylord Nelson, inspired in part by the 1969 Santa Barbara oil spill, organized a national teach-in on the environment. About 20 million Americans took part in the first one.
holidays.funFact: Earth Day is now observed in more than 190 countries and is often called the largest secular observance in the world. In 2009 the United Nations officially named it International Mother Earth Day.

holidays.name: National Jelly Bean Day
holidays.description: A day for sugar fans to enjoy the little bean-shaped candies, from classic cherry to the dreaded earwax and booger flavors.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday that grew out of the candy's long popularity. Jelly beans have been tied to Easter celebrations since the early 20th century, and the date often falls near the holiday.
holidays.funFact: Jelly beans made it into space in 1981 when the Space Shuttle crew was sent some. President Ronald Reagan famously kept a jar on his desk and handed them out at meetings.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Covered Cashew Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the crunchy, creamy, chocolatey snack that makes a handful of nuts feel like a fancy dessert.
holidays.origin: An unofficial snack holiday invented by food enthusiasts and snack makers, and promoted on food calendars as a reason to enjoy the sweet and salty combo.
holidays.funFact: Cashews are technically seeds that grow hanging from the bottom of a cashew apple. They are never sold in the shell because the shell contains a skin-irritating oil related to the one in poison ivy.

holidays.name: Girl Scout Leader's Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the volunteers who guide scouts through camping trips, badge projects, and the high-stakes business of cookie sales.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States each year on April 22 to honor the adults who lead troops. It recognizes the volunteer work behind the organization founded by Juliette Gordon Low in 1912.
holidays.funFact: The first Girl Scout cookies were baked at home in the 1910s and 1920s. Troops sold them to raise money, long before the organization began working with commercial bakers.

holidays.name: National Take a Chance Day
holidays.description: A day that urges you to step out of your comfort zone, try the weird menu item, send the risky text, or finally take that leap you keep putting off.
holidays.origin: An unofficial motivational observance that appears on lists of quirky holidays, encouraging people to embrace a little risk and spontaneity.
holidays.funFact: The word chance traces back to the Old French word for a fall of the dice, so the holiday's name is quite literally about rolling the dice.
